speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a longstanding pruritic rash accompanied by numbness and tingling in your palms. To begin our assessment, can you describe exactly how the rash looks and whether it appears on the backs of your hands or feet as well?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Leishmaniasis (specifically Diffuse Cutaneous Leishmaniasis or Post-Kala-Azar Dermal Leishmaniasis) due to exposure in a rice farming region with livestock contact. The combination of chronic, itchy, widespread rash and peripheral neuropathy (numbness/tingling) in a patient from an endemic area is highly suggestive of visceral leishmaniasis with secondary dermal involvement or direct cutaneous leishmaniasis with nerve compression. I will now request a Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) for Leishmaniasis and a complete blood count (CBC) to check for pancytopenia, which is common in visceral forms.
